correctness.rationale: Fourier covariance sends the source zero set to \(A^{-T}\mathcal N(P_{12})\). Using the twelve nearest source zeros in six unoriented midpoint lines spaced by \(\pi/6\), one line lies within \(\pi/12\) of the minor singular axis of \(A^{-T}\). Resolving that vector into singular directions gives the displayed factor. Factoring the comparison with one using \(q=s^2\) yields \(\sin^2(\pi/12)(q-1)(q-\cot^2(\pi/12))\), so strict decrease holds exactly for \(1<s<2+\sqrt3\) within this certificate. The endpoint/orientation sharpness is correctly limited to the twelve-zero witness method.
